source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: The suitability and placement of the series resistors on the I2C bus are still unclear to me.

ambiguity.description: Whether the I2C series resistors should be retained and where they should be placed is unresolved.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Either option is acceptable: remove the 44Ω resistors if they complicate the layout, or leave them in place if they are already fitted and not obstructing anything.

Those resistors on SDA/SCL are only there for signal quality. Because I2C lines are open-drain, releasing them requires the pull-up resistor to recharge the cable capacitance to 3.3V. That can produce slight overshoot or ringing at the transition edge, which the series resistance damps.

With our 20–40cm cables and 4.4kΩ pull-ups, rise time will remain well within specification, so this should not be a meaningful problem.

value_updates.series_resistor_population_policy: Remove the resistors if they complicate layout; otherwise they may remain when already fitted and unobstructive.
value_updates.series_resistor_purpose: Damp SDA/SCL transition overshoot or ringing for signal quality.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: That's correct. I'll send the revised document soon, and thanks for pointing out the placement issue.

value_updates.series_resistor_topology: Connect each series resistor directly to its ESP32-S3 I2C pin, with the pull-up and bus devices on the far side.
